record.question:
A company wants to rightsize a large fleet of memory-intensive EC2 database instances and attached EBS volumes. Many databases use active/passive failover pairs, and no representative utilization baseline exists. The company wants automated recommendations without committing to a support-plan upgrade.

Which action should the solutions architect take first?

options.text: Use current CPU utilization to identify lightly used instances and immediately downsize every passive database to the smallest available instance type.
Enable EC2 detailed monitoring and assume it automatically supplies guest memory and filesystem usage, then downsize instances after twelve hours.

Configure the CloudWatch agent to publish supported guest memory metrics, opt in to Compute Optimizer, and collect representative history. Review eligible EC2 and EBS recommendations against active/passive roles, peaks and tested failover capacity.
Purchase Enterprise Support, wait twelve hours for Trusted Advisor recommendations, and apply every suggested reduction without collecting additional workload history.

explanation.text:
<<3>> is correct. Compute Optimizer uses utilization history to generate recommendations, and supported memory metrics improve the evidence for memory-intensive workloads. Configure the agent and required metric dimensions; installation alone is insufficient.

<<1>> equates idle standby utilization with low required failover capacity. <<2>> confuses finer standard EC2 metric intervals with collection of guest memory data. <<4>> adds an unnecessary prerequisite and treats a short observation period as enough evidence for every workload.

For EC2, the documented minimum is 30 hours of CloudWatch data in the usual 14-day lookback. Passing that threshold does not prove a period represents business peaks. A standby must still sustain the active workload after failure. Validate memory, I/O, licensing and recovery requirements before applying changes, and distinguish recommendation eligibility from safe operational sizing.

AWS documentation (checked 2026-09-18):
https://docs.aws.amazon.com/compute-optimizer/latest/ug/requirements.html
https://docs.aws.amazon.com/compute-optimizer/latest/ug/ec2-metrics-analyzed.html
https://docs.aws.amazon.com/compute-optimizer/latest/ug/what-is-compute-optimizer.html

diagram_alt: The minimum metric threshold, representative workload coverage and standby capacity are separate requirements for safe rightsizing.

sources.supports: EC2 requires at least 30 hours of CloudWatch data over the standard 14-day lookback; resource types have separate requirements.
Compute Optimizer accepts supported CloudWatch-agent memory metrics with the InstanceId dimension.
Compute Optimizer is opted into and analyzes workload metrics to provide resource optimization recommendations.

editorial_notes: Removed false automatic-memory and twelve-hour claims; preserved the passive-database capacity caveat.
